name: module
title: Thin RP2040 module
orientation: A circuit board, made by a fab (JLCPCB), not printed. Seen from above: USB-C on the top long edge, castellated pins along the bottom edge and up both ends, the right end in an SPI display's order. Parts on the front, test points on the back.

edge_pins.rule: Pins along the bottom long edge, centred: SWITCH, GPIO20 to 23, 26 to 29 and 0 to 8, with a GND at each end (with open_pins, 24, 10 and 11 too)
edge_pins.label: Long-edge pins

end_pins.rule: Pins up each short end, from the corner
end_pins.label: End pins

end_rise.rule: Each end's lowest pin this far above the bottom edge: down at the corner, as on Waveshare's RP2040-Zero, its pad's top level with the tips of the long edge's pads (the design checks it against Sea-Picro's pads)

row_in.rule: The long edge's first and last pins this far in from the ends: their pads a pin's usual gap (a pitch less a pad's width, 0.84 mm) past the end of the corner pins' pads (the design checks it against Sea-Picro's pads)

pitch.rule: Pin pitch: 0.1 in headers, as Sea-Picro's

headers.rule: 1: each pin also has Sea-Picro's 0.1 in header hole and long pad beside its half hole, for pin headers or a sturdier joint. 0: half holes only, to solder flat: they reach less far into the board, which then needs less room across
headers.label: Header holes

show_headers.rule: 1: the 3D model shows a pin header in each header hole (a square pin and its plastic spacer under the board), as when the module is fitted with headers. The board itself is the same
show_headers.label: Show pin headers

key_pitch.rule: Keys' spacing on the keyboard the module mounts under: MX and most others, 0.75 in

span.rule: The end columns slot between keys: their header holes this many key widths apart (3: across a 2u Backspace and the 1u key beside it, or any three 1u keys)
span.label: Columns span

hole_in.rule: A header hole's centre in from its edge, with Sea-Picro's pads (the design checks it)

length.rule: Board length: the end columns' header holes span key widths, so their pins slot between switches
length.label: Length

height.rule: Board height, bottom edge to top edge: the room the core and the tracks round it need (2 mm more with header holes, whose pads reach farther in)
height.label: Height

core_turn.rule: Sea-Picro's core (the RP2040, flash, crystal, regulator and their small parts) turned as one block: its busiest side of escapes (RP2040 pins 2 to 12) faces the long row of pins

core_x.rule: The core block moved along the board: a channel from the end pins for tracks to pass

core_y.rule: The core block moved across the board: clear of the bottom pins (higher with header holes, which reach farther in), with room above it for tracks

usb_x.rule: USB-C socket along the top edge, from the middle: right of the core, its fuse and CC resistors under it
usb_x.label: USB-C position

usb_out.rule: The mid-mount socket's centre beyond the top edge, as on Sea-Picro

notch_below.rule: Reading Sea-Picro's notch: outline points this far below its top edge are the notch's

notch_reach.rule: Reading Sea-Picro's notch: outline points this near the socket, across the board

led_x.rule: Pad 32 (LED_5V, a 5 V supply for LEDs) under the USB parts

hole_d.rule: Mounting holes: for M2 screws, as the Raspberry Pi Pico's (2.1 mm)

hole_keepout.rule: Mounting holes: no track within this of a hole's centre (a 3.0 mm clear circle; an M2 screw head, 3.8 mm across, overlaps solder mask past it: use a nylon screw or washer). Wider keepouts crowd the tracks to the right-hand pins

hole_a_x.rule: First mounting hole, along the board from the middle: in the clear space between the core and the USB-C parts

hole_a_y.rule: First mounting hole, across the board from the middle

hole_b_x.rule: Second mounting hole, along the board: right of the LED5V pad, clear of the end pins' labels

hole_b_y.rule: Second mounting hole, across the board

switch_in.rule: R4 (SWITCH's resistor) in from its pin's castellated hole: clear of the header pad if there is one, within its placement rule

switch_turn.rule: R4 turned to lie across the board when its pin is on the long edge

display_gnd_front.rule: The right end matches an SPI display's header (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, RES, DC, CS, BLK). 1: GND at the front (the corner by the bottom row), BLK at the back; 0: the other way round, for a display mounted facing the other way

display_scl.rule: Display column: SCL (SPI clock): GPIO14, the RP2040's SPI1 clock

display_sda.rule: Display column: SDA (SPI data out): GPIO15, SPI1's data out

display_res.rule: Display column: RES (the display's reset): GPIO16

display_dc.rule: Display column: DC (data or command): GPIO12

display_cs.rule: Display column: CS (chip select): GPIO13, SPI1's own chip select

display_blk.rule: Display column, 8th pin: BLK (an LCD's backlight): GPIO9; any RP2040 pin can dim it by PWM. A 7-pin OLED leaves it free

open_pins.rule: 1: five more pins, for reset, boot and GPIO10, 11 and 24, left unjoined: their signals start inside Sea-Picro's kept routing round the RP2040, where the autorouter finds no way out, so their tracks are for drawing by hand (in KiCad, moving some of Sea-Picro's aside). 0: left off; the left end's top two places stay empty

row_gnd.rule: 1: a GND pin at each end of the bottom row, in the space by the corners (two more pins than Sea-Picro's, joined to its GND plane). 0: left off. With open_pins there's no room for them: set 0

layers.rule: Copper layers, as Sea-Picro's: tracks outside, GND and 3.3 V planes inside

track.rule: Signal track width: over JLCPCB's minimum, as Sea-Picro's fine tracks

clearance.rule: Copper to copper, kept by the router: Sea-Picro's own clearance (at JLCPCB's 0.1 mm the router packs tracks tighter and breaks more)

label_gap.rule: Pin labels: from the end of the header pad to the label

label_char.rule: Pin labels: a character's width, as a share of its height (tscircuit's font)

label_turn.rule: Pin labels along the long edge turned to run up from their pins
